To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the s-wave ρ-meson spectral function in symmetric nuclear matter is strongly modified by the nuclear medium and that it is dominated by a broad ρ-meson state with a mass of 600 MeV and width 500 MeV, while the s-wave ω-meson spectral function is not much modified by nuclear medium and is dominated by the ω-meson state with the free-space mass of 782 MeV and a small width.

(a) The ρ-meson spectral function in the nuclear medium has an enhancement in the ρ-mass region, which is due to the ρ-ππ and ρ-KK loops and the ρN interaction, (b) The ω-meson spectral function is not significantly modified in the medium, and (c) The ω-mesons are strongly suppressed by the ρ-ω mixing.
the ρ-meson spectral function is significantly modified in nuclear matter, while the ω-meson is not.
